summary: Manage persistent node seeds and distinguish chain health from network membership
details: Add peers list/add/remove/status/apply to the node kit with shared enode validation for IPv4, bracketed IPv6 and DNS, preserving distinct endpoints for one node identity.

Queue seed edits during bootstrap or an existing mining transition; apply with a durable journal and recreate only an already running chain, preserving upstream services, chain data and existing mining authorization.

Recover partial configuration/authorization writes, reject external drift, and require explicit apply to retry a failed target container. Down preserves seed intent without implicitly resuming services.
Report SEED_REQUIRED or WAITING_FOR_PEERS instead of claiming readiness from an idle genesis; retain the acknowledged first-node exception only for its bound data and node identity.

IPv6 container networking, endpoint failover and early mining intent with automatic synchronization gates remain subsequent phases. Basic CONNECTED status is not a common-height hash verification or mining authorization.
operator_actions: After installing the updated node kit, use peers add ENODE for joiners missing a persistent seed, then peers status --watch to observe application and connection. Seed changes on running nodes briefly restart only chain.
Resolve any peer operation error before peers apply. Wait for application and existing mining preflight gates before mining enable; use --first-node only for the acknowledged network founder.
